description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of different relational association categories evaluated in the MMRA benchmark for large visual language models, with each slice corresponding to a specific relational type and its frequency or count out of a total of 1024 instances (inferred from the sum of all values). The chart contains ten distinct categories, each labeled with its name, count, and percentage of the total. The largest segment is “ObservationAngle” at 126 instances (12.28%), followed by “SimilarMaterial” at 106 (10.33%), and “SubEvent” and “UsageSimilarity” both at 100 (9.74% and 9.65% respectively). Several categories — “SimilarEvent,” “AppearanceSimilarity,” “Environment,” and “Layout” — are tied at 90 instances each (8.77%). “MentalitySimilarity” accounts for 89 (8.67%), “RelativePosition” for 81 (7.90%), and “NearSameEntity” is the smallest segment at 63 (6.34%). The slices are color-coded with distinct hues (e.g., teal, orange, red, blue, gray) and are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right, with no exploded segments or additional annotations beyond the labels inside each slice. The chart provides a clear comparative view of how frequently each relational association type appears in the benchmark dataset.
